subject.title: [Bug P2] scheduleReconnect() has no max retry limit — infinite reconnect loop

question: Should GatewayClient keep unlimited reconnects by default and expose an opt-in cap only for selected short-lived callers, or should OpenClaw change the default reconnect policy globally?
rationale: The source-level loop is clear, but node-host currently relies on unlimited reconnect recovery, so the permanent retry contract is a compatibility and product-policy decision.

options.title: Opt-in bounded reconnect
options.body: Keep node-host unlimited by default, add a package-level cap option, and wire it only into maintainer-approved short-lived clients with proof for capped and default behavior.

options.title: Global retry cap
options.body: Make every GatewayClient stop after a fixed number of attempts, accepting the risk that long-lived node hosts no longer recover automatically after extended outages.

options.title: Document unlimited retries
options.body: Keep current behavior as intentional recovery policy and document the resource-risk tradeoff instead of adding a retry ceiling.

recommendation.title: Opt-in bounded reconnect
recommendation.body: Keep node-host unlimited by default, add a package-level cap option, and wire it only into maintainer-approved short-lived clients with proof for capped and default behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The original Gateway WebSocket control-plane behavior and historical retry policy trace most directly through this owner path.
